name: Phagshapa
instructions: 1. Slice the pork fat or belly into strips and sauté in a pot until the fat renders out and the edges turn light brown.
2. Add crushed ginger and garlic to the rendered fat and sauté until fragrant.
3. Incorporate the dried red chilies and turmeric powder, stirring briefly to release the spice oils.
4. Add thick wedges or slices of radish to the pot and toss well to coat.
5. Pour in enough water to cover the ingredients, season with salt, and simmer covered on low heat until the radish is tender and the pork is succulent.
6. Continue cooking until the liquid reduces to a thick, flavorful gravy-like consistency.
description: Phagshapa is a quintessential Sikkimese delicacy, deeply rooted in the Himalayan lifestyle. It is a hearty, fat-rich stew traditionally served with rice or rotis, prized for its ability to provide warmth and sustenance in cold mountain climates.
